About

Wool

Fine, creamy and highly prized by hand-spinners and textile artists.

OverviewHistoryWoolFor the Table

Fleece Characteristics

Portland wool is one of the finest produced by any British primitive breed. The fleece has a characteristic warm creamy-white colour with a soft, dense texture and a moderate staple length of around 5–8 cm. The fibre diameter typically ranges from 27–33 microns — finer than many Down breeds and comparable to some Merino crosses.

The natural crimp gives the spun yarn excellent elasticity and bounce. Portland wool takes dye beautifully, producing rich, even colours that make it popular with natural dyers working with plant-based dyes.

Fleece Weight

Average fleece weight is modest — typically 1–2 kg per ewe — reflecting the breed's small size and efficient conversion. What the Portland lacks in bulk it more than makes up for in quality.

Uses

  • Hand-spinning: The staple length and crimp make it ideal for hand-spinning, either from raw fleece or as prepared roving. It spins to a smooth, well-defined yarn.
  • Knitting and weaving: Portland yarn produces garments with excellent drape and warmth-to-weight ratio.
  • Natural dyeing: The creamy white base takes plant dyes exceptionally well.
  • Felt-making: The fine crimp allows good felting for both wet and needle felt work.

Shearing

Portland sheep are typically shorn once a year in late spring or early summer. The fleece should be skirted promptly after shearing to remove heavily soiled edges, then stored in a cool, dry, well-ventilated space.

Members of the Portland Sheep Breeders' Group frequently offer raw fleeces for sale via the Marketplace. Fleece classes are also offered at the Group's Premier Shows.

Showing Fleece

Portland fleeces are judged on fineness, staple length, colour, cleanliness and overall presentation. See our Showing pages for full guidance on preparing and presenting a fleece for competition.
